prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by bifunctional molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase, and for the structure-guided ligand design that made the mechanism general

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B028 (Gray and Winkler) to B034, restricted to the PROTAC branch with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. After round 1 I have to take the evidence as it stands. B028 is mature and its physics is sound, but nobody else ranked it and the objections from Aili and Zou on breadth and new capability were not answered by anything I can point to. B034 is the candidate where the mechanism is best defined at the level I care about: formation of a ternary complex, cooperativity, and ubiquitin transfer to a chosen substrate, reproduced independently by many groups. It turns a cellular process into a designable chemical reaction. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and the first demonstrations. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned the concept into a general, structure-guided design rule, which is what makes it chemistry and not only pharmacology. This is three names, one coherent achievement, and the configuration with the widest opening and round-1 backing among my own earlier ranks (I ranked it fourth, and it is the most-cited alternative after B011).
statement.case_against: The credit question is not settled and I may be wrong on Handa. Cereblon and the molecular-glue mechanism is a separate achievement with the longest patient record, and a citation that ignores it may look incomplete to Chabes and Sparr, while a citation that includes it risks crediting two discoveries as one. The clinical verdict on PROTACs is early, with no approved degrader, so maturity rests on mechanism and tool use and not on medicines. Ciulli over Sakamoto and Kim, who did the earliest PROTAC experiments, is a judgement about which step is decisive that I cannot verify from the files and want the expert reports to confirm. I also give up B028, where my field proximity makes me an unreliable advocate anyway, and B011, which has the cleanest attribution, is a real rival to this configuration.

responses.point: Chabes prefers B034 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, treating the cereblon glue arm as the strongest evidence of maturity and the PROTAC arm as the generalisable design principle.
responses.response: I now join you on B034, but not on the trio. Your own argument shows why the glue arm is the better matured one, and that is exactly why I think it deserves its own citation and not a third seat in a PROTAC prize. If the committee wants the glue arm it should credit it for what it is, and the three-person cap makes that impossible alongside Crews and Deshaies. Where I agree with you is that this is the best mechanistically defined candidate on the list. I would accept Handa in place of Ciulli if the expert reports show that cereblon is the decisive step, but I want that stated in the citation and not left implicit.

responses.point: Aili prefers B034 (Crews and Deshaies) paired with base editing for Liu, argues that a designable chemical modality matters more than a textbook mechanism, and says he would not strongly defend the Handa boundary.
responses.response: Your test of whether the work changed what others can do is fair, and it is the reason I moved off B028. I agree with Crews and Deshaies as the core and with your readiness to leave Handa out. I differ in adding Ciulli as the third name, because structure-guided ligand design is what made proximity-induced degradation a general method for chemists. On pairing it with base editing, I would not add B012. The three-person limit leaves one place, and I see Liu's work as protein engineering of an existing deaminase, following closely on the 2020 CRISPR prize.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B011 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the cleanest attribution, fully mature, with a chemistry-driven reversible-terminator invention.
responses.response: I agree that your pair is the cleanest credit on the list and I keep B011 as my second alternative. I still hesitate on the question the chair posed, which is whether a citation can reward the reversible-terminator chemistry and not the sequencing field. Your wording does that better than most. My difficulty is that the patent and priority history is not yet separated from the science, and I want the expert reports to say which step is the chemical invention. If they do, B011 and B034 are close for me, and I would not resist if the committee moves to B011.

responses.point: Linke prefers B011 (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) with a second part for Bayley alone on nanopores, and the chair asks whether B001 can be defended with a living set of names.
responses.response: I would answer the chair's question by saying that I cannot support B001 as proposed. Bayley alone omits Deamer and Akeson, whose strand-level discrimination and enzyme ratcheting are the sequencing step, and a three-name set would need Bayley's status and the Branton question confirmed first. Two DNA-reading parts would also use your whole three-person allowance on one theme, a field prize more than a discovery. If you want a second part I would rather see you keep B011 as a single part, which I could accept.

responses.point: Sparr finds the two-name attribution for B028 persuasive but ranks condensates (B026) higher because its reach in the molecular life sciences is wider, and she would support B028 in a two-part prize if numbers allowed.
responses.response: Thank you for the generous reading of B028. I accept that the numbers do not allow it and that I cannot ask you to give up names in B026 to make room. I do not rank B026 above B034 because the in vivo evidence, which you and Linke both describe as uneven, is less settled than the ternary-complex mechanism. I would also want the committee to decide whether the physical chemistry in condensates is new, given the older polymer theory. I would revisit it if the expert reports speak strongly to functional condensates in cells.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat B034 as one achievement or two, and whether Handa and cereblon are decisive enough to displace Ciulli from the third place.
Whether Sakamoto and Kim's early PROTAC work should count above Ciulli's structure-guided ligand design for the credit.
Whether an unapproved PROTAC record makes B034 premature this year, in which case B011 is the safer configuration.
Whether the reversible-terminator step in B011 can be separated cleanly from 454, Lynx and Mayer's colony work.
statement.conflict_note: My earlier disclosure of field proximity to B028 no longer matters for my preferred configuration, since B028 is now only an alternative, and I will rely on the expert reports for it. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies or Ciulli as far as my profile shows. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who has offered recusal on B051, and I see no conflict in that.
